Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Tihansh usually hope their child will grow to embody god of the earth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Tihansh is a name of Lord Vishnu, the preserver in the Hindu Trimurti. It represents the power and strength of the divine, as well as the stability and loyalty that comes from being rooted in the earth.
data.etymology: Tihansh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of the Earth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tihansh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.
